The Dutch are an awesome people, I studied there for a year and had no problems speaking English and making friends. My tip would be, make sure you go to city Hall ASAP and get registered there, the university will likely have a page on that. Public transport is very good and is quite cheap for a person on a European income, obviously your financial situation may be different so I'd recommend getting a bike and you'll be able to get anywhere in the city in like 30 mins. It's a great place, I hope you enjoy!

I know it's maybe not what you want to hear but speak to an immigration lawyer/specialist, most have a free consultation so you can decide to go forward if you need. Good thing is you've got plenty of time to get what you need done. Good luck!

Once you have an address if you plan to stay in the Nethlands for more than 4 months you need to register, [this](https://www.iamexpat.nl/expat-info/official-issues/registration-netherlands) explains it pretty well. Then you get your BSN which you need for basically everything.

items.title: Books with a really good villain/motive for someone to be the "bad guy" or more complex antagonists.
items.text:
Books with a really good villain/motive for someone to be the "bad guy" or more complex antagonists.
Looking for something with an amazing antagonist.


I don't read much fiction, but when I do I get super bored when the antagonist has motivations that make no sense. Basically they're just bad because "errr well we need a story so I guess we gotta have a bad man who loves money and power so he would kill his own son with a spoon for $20 and we should shoot him on the spot if we see him." Obviously an exaggeration, but looking for something a bit more subtle and complex.
